newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea moving copper stocks overseas to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea moving copper stocks overseas to cut costs.

text.p: South Korea's continuing economic slowdown has forced domestic copper end-users and traders to ship their stocks overseas to cut carrying costs, traders in Seoul said.
They said the economy has also caused copper import premiums for grade A to fall recently to $50-$60 a tonne from $80-$85 due to lack of demand.
"We are asking local traders to ship our stocks overseas," a trader with a local cable maker said.
Traders said several copper buyers were seen asking their suppiers to delay shipping schedules.
A trader with a local trading house said more than 2,000 tonnes of grade A copper were said to have been shipped recently from South Korea to China and Singapore.
The domestic aluminium market was seen worsening as more small- and medium-sized metal companies have recently defaulted on debt repayments, traders said.
"Under this circumstance, no one wants to sell metals to small companies. It is too risky," said a trader with a major trading house.

However, the domestic aluminium market appeared to be experiencing a slight shortage since most traders have reduced their inventories in the second quarter due to heavy carrying costs amid the economic slump, traders said.
They said most aluminium buyers also delayed purchases for their third quarter requirements on expectations of lower import premiums in the quarter.
But the premiums were set at around $95 a tonne for the third quarter shipment, compared to $88 a tonne in the second quarter.
Aluminium import premiums for spot delivery remained firm at $95-$100 a tonnes CIF Pusan over LME's cash prices, traders said.
Domestic aluminium prices rose to 1,550,000-1,560,000 won a tonne due to unusual supply tightness in the domestic market from 1,540,000 won a week ago, they said.
Domestic copper prices were flat at 2,467,000 won a tonne over the past week and zinc prices were also unchanged at 1,348,000 won.
